extraction.name: Pointer Sentinel Mixture Models
extraction.description: A neural sequence model architecture combining pointer networks and softmax classifiers to improve language modeling performance, particularly for rare or unseen words. Introduces the WikiText corpus for evaluating long-range dependencies and realistic vocabularies.
extraction.creator: Stephen Merity, Caiming Xiong, James Bradbury, Richard Socher
extraction.citeAs: Merity, S., Xiong, C., Bradbury, J., & Socher, R. (2016). Pointer Sentinel Mixture Models. arXiv:1609.07843.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Text extracted from Wikipedia articles meeting Good or Featured article criteria, processed to remove lists, mathematical formulae, and other non-textual elements. Normalization and tokenization performed using Moses tokenizer with additional fixes.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Wikipedia articles meeting Good or Featured article criteria, extracted via Wikipedia API. Raw text includes Wikipedia markup macros which were cleaned during processing.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Replacement of numbers with 'N', newlines with 'heosi', punctuation removal, lowercasing, and mapping of out-of-vocabulary words to 'hunkitoken'. Mathematical formulae replaced with 'hformulaitokens'.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Tokenization using Moses tokenizer with augmented number splitting. Vocabulary constructed by discarding words with count below 3. Words outside vocabulary mapped to 'hunkitoken'. Dataset formatted to match Penn Treebank conventions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: No human annotation protocol described; dataset consists of raw text from Wikipedia articles.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Dataset made freely available to the community via WikiText dataset site. No explicit versioning or deprecation policy mentioned.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Dataset may contain biases inherent in Wikipedia content, including potential underrepresentation of certain topics or demographic groups. The Good/Featured article criteria may introduce selection bias toward well-established topics.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limited to Wikipedia content, which may not represent all domains of language use. Preprocessing steps (e.g., lowercasing, punctuation removal) may limit applicability for tasks requiring original formatting. Vocabulary cutoff at 3 occurrences may exclude rare but meaningful terms.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, and Validation for language modeling tasks, particularly those requiring handling of rare words and long-range dependencies. Designed for benchmarking neural sequence models.
